about.title: Rialto Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: When you check into a hospital or sit down in an exam room in Rialto, you expect the people caring for you to follow the basic standards of their profession. Sometimes they don't, and the result is a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, or a medication that should never have been given. In a San Bernardino County city of roughly 103,000 people, the aftermath of a preventable error can follow you home for years. California handles these claims under MICRA, and its rules differ from ordinary injury cases: the clock generally runs one year from when you discovered the harm and no more than three years from the injury itself, a 90-day notice must go out before filing, and non-economic damages are capped at a figure that rises every year. Nearly every case also needs a qualified medical expert to explain what went wrong. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm; we connect Rialto residents with an independent attorney who takes malpractice claims on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was taken to the hospital after a crash on SR-210 and something went wrong during treatment. Is that a car accident claim or a malpractice claim?
items.answer: It may be both, and they are handled differently. Rialto recorded 432 injury collisions in 2025, and crash patients sometimes suffer separate harm from an error in the emergency room or during follow-up care. The driver claim falls under ordinary negligence rules, while the medical error falls under MICRA with its own deadlines and notice requirement. An attorney can sort out which facts belong to which claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice case in California?
items.answer: Generally one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and never more than three years from the date the injury occurred. Before filing, you must also send the provider a 90-day notice of intent to sue. Because these windows are shorter than most injury claims, it is wise to get your records reviewed promptly.

items.question: Does a poor result from my surgery mean the surgeon committed malpractice?
items.answer: Not by itself. Medicine carries known risks, and a disappointing outcome only becomes malpractice when a provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and that failure caused your harm. California courts almost always require a qualified medical expert to establish this. A contingency attorney from our network can arrange that review and tell you frankly where your Rialto case stands.
